details.description: gpt-rosalind-research (GPT-Rosalind) is OpenAI's dedicated life sciences reasoning model, combining frontier reasoning with specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance and other scientific applications. It powers Rosalind Workbench, a research-preview environment in the ChatGPT app that gives scientists a guided, connected view from a biological question through data, analysis and evidence. API access to gpt-rosalind-research is limited to approved organizations through OpenAI's trusted-access program, and billing for it is scheduled to begin October 5, 2026.
advantages: OpenAI describes it as its dedicated life sciences model, combining frontier reasoning with specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance and other scientific applications (OpenAI Rosalind Workbench blog post).

Powers Rosalind Workbench's guided scientific workflows, including a molecular structure viewer, a biological sequence and alignment viewer, and a pathology slide viewer that keep the request, analysis and evidence connected in one conversation (OpenAI Rosalind Workbench blog post).
OpenAI states that all eligible organizations will continue to get access to the latest GPT-Rosalind models as they are released (OpenAI pricing page).
disadvantages: API access is limited to approved organizations through OpenAI's trusted-access program rather than being generally available (OpenAI pricing page).
Rosalind Workbench, the primary way this model is used, is still in research preview through the ChatGPT app (OpenAI Rosalind Workbench blog post).
OpenAI has not published a dedicated model-card page, context window or output-token limit for gpt-rosalind-research (OpenAI Models and pricing pages).
use_cases: Guided scientific research workflows connecting a biological question to genomic, structural and literature evidence
Molecular structure analysis, such as inspecting a protein-ligand complex from a PDB file
Biological sequence and alignment analysis, such as comparing protein variants

sources.title: Meet Rosalind Workbench: Empowering every scientist to be their own research team | OpenAI Developers

notes: OpenAI has no dedicated /api/docs/models/gpt-rosalind-research page (404); it appears only in the models overview list ('Life sciences reasoning for approved organizations') and the pricing page's specialized-models table, which links out to the Rosalind Workbench blog post for the product description used here. Catalog's max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens are empty and no context/output limit is published anywhere found, so none is stated. Catalog modality is text_input/text_output only; could not confirm on an opened page whether the raw API model itself accepts image input (Workbench's own viewers handle images/structures), so modality was left as given rather than guessed.
